title: SLO variance attribution and corrective-action catalog (2025)
author: Asha Kapoor
body:
> **Archived 2025-09-15:** this page is superseded by "SLO variance attribution and corrective-action catalog" and is kept for reference only.

Summary:
A single repeatable process for attributing SLO variance, classifying the root cause, and mapping each variance class to a prescribed corrective action (operational, capacity, product, or process). It brings together attribution heuristics, an error-budget burn matrix, an on-call runbook for rapid burns, evidence requirements for SLO regressions, and the telemetry/tooling standards needed to automate attribution.

Goals:
- Shorten time-to-remediation for SLO breaches and fast error-budget burns.
- Make scale / throttle / rollback / credit decisions consistent and evidence-led.
- Keep runbook steps short for common variance classes.
- Feed corrective actions into capacity planning and product backlogs.

Scope:
- All customer-facing inference endpoints and internal model training APIs with an SLO.
- Three windows: rolling-1h, rolling-1d, and 28-day (monthly, contractual SLAs).
- Excludes ad-hoc load tests and synthetic-only canaries.

Key definitions:
- SLO target: declared p99/p95/median latency, success-rate, or availability objective.
- Error budget: 1 - SLO.
- Burn rate: current error rate / allowed error rate over a window (e.g., 1h).
- Variance: measured deviation from expected SLO.
- Attribution: evidence-based assignment of variance to a primary cause class.

Workflow:
1) Detection: burn-rate alert fires.
2) Evidence capture: automated snapshot.
3) Automated attribution: slo-attrib heuristics.
4) Human validation: oncall confirms primary cause in the incident ticket.
5) Corrective action: runbook mitigation now, follow-up in backlog.

Attribution categories:
- Traffic spike (legitimate demand): more requests on upstream API keys, normal token distribution, unchanged origin IPs and request sizes. Evidence: per-tenant QPS > 3x baseline at legitimate times. Action: admit capacity within reserved/dedicated tiers, otherwise throttle non-critical lanes.
- Misbehaving client / broken SDK change: abrupt request-shape changes, malformed requests, new user-agent or SDK version. Action: targeted throttle or block by API key; contact the partner; open a postmortem.
- Model-serving regression: higher per-token latency, KV-cache miss spikes, quantization fallbacks, OOMs. Evidence: runtime tail traces, GPU host metrics, rollout timeline. Action: roll back to the previous verified variant or divert to a warm lower-cost variant.
- Infrastructure degradation: network errors, packet loss, disk IO, scheduler preemption. Action: pull hosts from rotation, scale across regions, activate burst pool.
- Cascade from a dependency (auth, key-store): correlated dependency errors. Action: circuit breaker to fail fast and protect serving.

Error-budget burn -> corrective-action matrix:

| Burn-rate (1h) | Likely classes | Immediate mitigations | Owner |
|---:|---|---|---|
| < 2x | Noise or minor spike | Monitor and collect evidence | Oncall |
| 2x - 4x | Traffic spike or client mutation | Burst pool; non-critical lane throttles; contact large tenants | Oncall + Capacity |
| 4x - 10x | Serving regression or infra degradation | Serving rollback; remove faulty hosts; escalate to runtime P0 | Oncall + Serving Runtime |
| > 10x or sustained 30m | Cascade or attack | Emergency degradation plan, customer credits evaluation | Incident lead + Eng leadership |

Service owners publish service-specific multipliers in their SLO doc.

Runbook: rapid error-budget burn (1h burn-rate alert)
1) Acknowledge alert within 10 minutes and attach the automated snapshot (request rate, top-20 tenants, tail latencies, GPU host metrics, recent deploys).
2) Run attribution: slo-attrib-cli explain --window=1h --top-tenants
3) Triage using the categories. If attribution returns >80% confidence, start the prescribed mitigation.
4) Suspected serving regression: check rollout notes (redwood-console/rollouts); if a rollout happened in the last 30m, roll back with redwood-deploy rollback --service <svc> --to-version <prev>; warm the alternative variant pool before shifting traffic.
5) Infrastructure: cordon and drain impacted hosts, then scale out in another failure domain.
6) Tenant traffic spike: contact top-impact tenants and enable per-tenant soft-throttle or rate-limit.
7) Record primary cause, confidence, and follow-up owner in the ticket.

Evidence requirements for SLO regressions:
- Metric snapshots for the detection window plus the preceding 2x window.
- Top-50 failing request samples (redacted) with tenant-id, user-agent, model variant.
- Span-level traces for tail requests.
- Deployment timeline for the last 60 minutes.
- Host logs (OOMs, kernel stalls, scheduler events) and provider network health.
- Attribution output and rationale.

Tooling standards:
- slo-attrib runs on every detection and outputs primary_cause, confidence (0-100), top tenants, metric deltas.
- Dashboards: per-service SLO overview (1h, 1d, 28d), per-tenant heatmap, model-variant tail latency.
- Alerts:
  - slo_burn_rate_1h > 2.0 -> PagerDuty P2 to oncall.
  - slo_burn_rate_1h > 4.0 -> PagerDuty P1 and notify runtime-oncall.
- PromQL:
  - burn_rate_1h: sum(rate(slo_error_total[1h])) / sum(rate(slo_allowed_errors[1h]))
  - top_tenants_by_errors: topk(20, sum by (tenant_id) (rate(slo_error_total[1h])))

Capacity planning integration:
- Each confirmed legitimate-demand spike gets a Capacity Request ticket: peak QPS, 95th token length, warm-cache ramp time, suggested GPU type, cost delta.
- Quarterly reliability digest of all attributions and corrective actions.

Service-owner responsibilities:
- Publish burn-rate multipliers and priority lane definitions.
- Dedicated services: configure the admission controller to favour contract tenants during global throttles.
- Validate automated attribution monthly and tune heuristics.

Post-incident checklist:
- Corrective-action epics linked to the incident.
- After a rollback: stricter canary thresholds, longer canaries, mandatory shadowing.
- After adding capacity: cost/benefit review with Finance within 30 days.
- Update detection signatures in the owner's playbook.

Governance:
- Monthly cross-functional attribution review (SRE, Serving Runtime, Product, Capacity).
- Quarterly reliability program with aggregated categories and investment recommendations.

Contact and ownership:
- Author: Asha Kapoor (SRE Reliability)
- Reviewer: Liam Chen (Serving Runtime)
